title: Reconstruction of a complete group from its discrete orbit functor
statement:
Let $G$ be a Hausdorff topological group whose identity has a basis of open subgroups. Assume that $G$ is compact, or complete for the two-sided uniformity: every net Cauchy for both $g_i^{-1}g_j$ and $g_ig_j^{-1}$ converges. Let $\mathcal O_G$ be the small category [def-nagata-category] with objects the left $G$-sets $G/U$ for open subgroups $U\subseteq G$, and with all $G$-equivariant maps as arrows. Give these sets the discrete topology. Write $\omega_G:\mathcal O_G\to\mathbf{Set}$ for the underlying-set functor. Topologize $\operatorname{Aut}(\omega_G)$ by pointwise convergence on all its underlying sets: basic identity neighborhoods fix finitely many specified elements of finitely many $G/U$. Then the map
$$G\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(\omega_G),\qquad g\longmapsto(s\longmapsto gs)_{G/U}$$
is an isomorphism of topological groups. Equivalently one obtains the same automorphism group and topology using the forgetful functor on all discrete continuous left $G$-sets; restriction to $\mathcal O_G$ induces this identification. Categories and sets are placed in compatible universes.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5, pp. 63–64, with Example 7.1.6 for the compact case; orbit-category formulation from the proof (the objects G/U determine a natural automorphism on all disjoint unions).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-orbit-translation-topological-embedding] to obtain the translation homomorphism $\Phi$, injective with its induced topology, and a topological group $\operatorname{Aut}(\omega_G)$. Fix $\alpha$ in that group. Apply [lem-sfb-orbit-automorphism-cauchy-realizers] to its tagged coordinate set $D$: obtain the net $g_F$, the closed coordinate cosets $C_x$, their finite intersection property, and the two-sided Cauchy condition.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5 and Example 7.1.6, printed pp. 63–64; assembly step 1 of the extracted arguments.

proof.text: In the complete alternative, the two-sided Cauchy net converges to some $g\in G$ by the hypothesis. For each coordinate $x$, the tail with $F\supseteq\{x\}$ lies in $C_x$. Closedness gives $g\in C_x$: otherwise the open complement, as a neighborhood of the limit, would eventually contain this same tail. Thus $gx=\alpha_U(x)$ on every $G/U$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5 and Example 7.1.6, printed pp. 63–64; assembly step 2 of the extracted arguments.

proof.text: In the compact alternative, apply [lem-sfb-compact-closed-finite-intersection] to $X=G$, $I=D$ and the closed sets $C_x$ from step 1. Its compactness hypothesis is the present alternative; its finite-intersection hypothesis, including the empty family, is exactly the Cauchy-realizers lemma. Obtain $g\in\bigcap_x C_x$, again satisfying $gx=\alpha_U(x)$ for every coordinate.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5 and Example 7.1.6, printed pp. 63–64; assembly step 3 of the extracted arguments.

proof.text: Under either alternative, equality at every coordinate gives $\Phi(g)=\alpha$, so $\Phi$ is surjective. Together with the embedding and homomorphism in step 1, this makes it an isomorphism of topological groups. Now apply [lem-sfb-orbit-reconstruction-extension]: its bijective-translation hypothesis has just been proved. It identifies restriction from all discrete continuous actions with a topological group isomorphism and sends $\Phi(g)$ back to translation by $g$ on every action, proving the final clause.
